summary: This is a mechanical, read-only registry-generation task: a new entity-relationship schema (WIRING_ENGINE_SCHEMA_2026-07-25.yaml), a generator script (generate_wiring_registry.py) that only reads existing JSON/YAML catalogs and a SQLite DB in read-only mode (no SQL string interpolation, no subprocess/exec calls, no command or path injection surface) and writes a single JSON snapshot, a phase plan document, a widened glob in auto_phase_continuation.py that is backward-compatible with existing plan files, and supporting registry/decision-log bookkeeping. No changes touch .github/workflows/**, auth/, payment/billing, migrations, schema.sql, or .env, consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification. The diff is additive and low-blast-radius, and the generator script is idempotent and side-effect-free beyond writing its own output file, so autonomous merge is reasonable.
issues: The new crontab entry (generate-wiring-registry, every 6h) is recorded in OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml with status 'approved' and approved_via citing the task's own dispatched SPEC asserting a standing 'blanket approval' rather than a fresh, independently verifiable Owner confirmation for this specific entry -- the task both raised and self-resolved this decision. It mirrors a stated prior precedent (two earlier crontab entries used the same pattern), but this self-approval mechanism is worth an Owner spot-check since it lets a worker task grant itself crontab-modification authority by citation alone.

ai-os/WIRING_ENGINE_REGISTRY_2026-07-25.json is a ~5MB, 169794-line generated snapshot committed directly to git. The generator script's own docstring states large machine-generated catalogs (DATABASE_CATALOG.json, FUNCTION_CATALOG.json, AI_ROSTER_CATALOG.json) are deliberately kept out of git for this exact reason ('too large, regenerated from live app code'), so committing this task's own equally-large output as a static, date-suffixed file is an inconsistent precedent -- if a future task starts periodically re-committing regenerated snapshots, this will bloat repository history for a file whose per-entity last_verified_ts timestamp changes on every run even absent real content changes.

Minor: the commit message, MASTER_INDEX.yaml entry, and task narrative all state '7642 entities' for the real run, but the committed JSON's own meta.entity_count is 7645 -- a small self-report accuracy discrepancy, not a functional defect.
